### [00:17:39.590 - 00:17:40.630]

between the raters

### [00:17:40.630 - 00:17:42.010]

to just align

### [00:17:42.010 - 00:17:43.750]

on how they should rate

### [00:17:43.750 - 00:17:44.950]

the answers.

### [00:17:46.010 - 00:17:48.090]

So it can be seen

### [00:17:48.090 - 00:17:50.430]

as just a health metric

### [00:17:50.430 - 00:17:51.410]

to track

### [00:17:51.410 - 00:17:52.830]

how consistent

### [00:17:52.830 - 00:17:53.710]

your rating are.

### [00:17:54.690 - 00:17:56.130]

And this is typically

### [00:17:56.130 - 00:17:57.210]

something that people use

### [00:17:57.210 - 00:17:58.630]

in practice.

### [00:18:00.920 - 00:18:03.380]

So up until now,

### [00:18:03.440 - 00:18:04.980]

we've seen one limitation

### [00:18:04.980 - 00:18:06.700]

of human ratings.

### [00:18:08.120 - 00:18:09.560]

Well, second limitation,

### [00:18:09.740 - 00:18:10.600]

I think I also said

### [00:18:10.600 - 00:18:11.160]

this previously.

### [00:18:11.160 - 00:18:12.820]

So it's really slow.

### [00:18:13.000 - 00:18:13.100]

You know,

### [00:18:13.140 - 00:18:14.160]

if you ask someone

### [00:18:14.160 - 00:18:16.200]

to rate 1,000 LM outputs,

### [00:18:16.460 - 00:18:17.740]

well, it will take them a while.

### [00:18:19.020 - 00:18:20.260]

And it's, of course, expensive.

### [00:18:22.450 - 00:18:24.110]

So all of that to say

### [00:18:24.110 - 00:18:27.230]

that our ideal scenario

### [00:18:27.230 - 00:18:29.670]

of asking a human

### [00:18:29.670 - 00:18:31.850]

to rate every LLM output

### [00:18:31.850 - 00:18:33.190]

is not something

### [00:18:33.190 - 00:18:33.890]

that is practical.

### [00:18:33.890 - 00:18:38.090]

but we can leverage

### [00:18:38.090 - 00:18:40.430]

human ratings

### [00:18:40.430 - 00:18:42.930]

in some way

### [00:18:42.930 - 00:18:43.770]

because we've seen

### [00:18:43.770 - 00:18:45.290]

that even if the task

### [00:18:45.290 - 00:18:45.890]

is subjective,

### [00:18:46.410 - 00:18:48.170]

we can have a way

### [00:18:48.170 - 00:18:49.590]

to align our raters.

### [00:18:51.270 - 00:18:53.090]

So now let's move on

### [00:18:53.090 - 00:18:55.150]

to another way

### [00:18:55.150 - 00:18:56.390]

to go about doing this,

### [00:18:56.590 - 00:18:58.050]

which is by using

### [00:18:58.050 - 00:18:59.730]

some rule-based metrics.

### [00:18:59.730 - 00:19:02.970]

So here I'm just going

### [00:19:02.970 - 00:19:04.610]

to revise the setting

### [00:19:04.610 - 00:19:05.630]

that I mentioned before.

### [00:19:06.710 - 00:19:08.450]

And instead of asking

### [00:19:08.450 - 00:19:09.670]

our humans

### [00:19:09.670 - 00:19:10.530]

to write

### [00:19:10.530 - 00:19:12.330]

every LLM output,

### [00:19:13.130 - 00:19:14.070]

this time

### [00:19:14.070 - 00:19:15.570]

I'm just going

### [00:19:15.570 - 00:19:16.290]

to ask them

### [00:19:16.290 - 00:19:17.670]

to write

### [00:19:17.670 - 00:19:20.490]

the references

### [00:19:20.490 - 00:19:22.210]

or the ideal output

### [00:19:22.210 - 00:19:23.870]

for a given set

### [00:19:23.870 - 00:19:24.330]

of prompts,

### [00:19:25.190 - 00:19:26.510]

just fix that for good,

### [00:19:27.350 - 00:19:29.730]

and then use

### [00:19:29.730 - 00:19:31.310]

some kind of metric

### [00:19:31.310 - 00:19:33.190]

that would compare

### [00:19:33.190 - 00:19:34.930]

the LLM outputs

### [00:19:34.930 - 00:19:36.910]

with those references.

### [00:19:39.880 - 00:19:41.300]

So here the main difference

### [00:19:41.300 - 00:19:42.840]

is let's suppose

### [00:19:42.840 - 00:19:44.340]

I have a given set

### [00:19:44.340 - 00:19:45.500]

of prompts fixed.

### [00:19:46.680 - 00:19:48.680]

Well, I can make iterations

### [00:19:48.680 - 00:19:49.380]

in my model

### [00:19:49.380 - 00:19:51.640]

and always compare

### [00:19:51.640 - 00:19:52.680]

the outputs

### [00:19:52.680 - 00:19:53.760]

of my LLM

### [00:19:53.760 - 00:19:55.120]

with this

### [00:19:55.120 - 00:19:56.660]

fixed reference

### [00:19:56.660 - 00:19:58.560]

instead of always

### [00:19:58.560 - 00:19:59.620]

asking humans

### [00:19:59.620 - 00:20:00.200]

to write that

### [00:20:00.200 - 00:20:00.840]

again and again.

### [00:20:01.520 - 00:20:02.300]

So it's already

### [00:20:02.300 - 00:20:02.740]

an improvement.

### [00:20:05.250 - 00:20:07.050]

And we will see

### [00:20:07.050 - 00:20:07.630]

a little bit

### [00:20:07.630 - 00:20:08.810]

what are the kinds

### [00:20:08.810 - 00:20:10.570]

of rule-based metrics

### [00:20:10.570 - 00:20:11.170]

that you will see

### [00:20:11.170 - 00:20:11.570]

out there.

### [00:20:14.140 - 00:20:16.020]

So ideally,

### [00:20:16.760 - 00:20:17.640]

these metrics

### [00:20:17.640 - 00:20:19.000]

should reflect

### [00:20:19.000 - 00:20:20.460]

the performance

### [00:20:20.460 - 00:20:22.080]

of the LLM output

### [00:20:22.080 - 00:20:24.460]

in an optimal way

### [00:20:24.460 - 00:20:25.080]

and what I mean

### [00:20:25.080 - 00:20:26.140]

by an optimal way

### [00:20:26.140 - 00:20:28.920]

is to make it

### [00:20:28.920 - 00:20:29.780]

be a little bit

### [00:20:29.780 - 00:20:30.280]

flexible

### [00:20:30.280 - 00:20:31.940]

given the fact

### [00:20:31.940 - 00:20:33.820]

that natural language

### [00:20:33.820 - 00:20:35.380]

is not always

### [00:20:35.380 - 00:20:36.140]

something that

### [00:20:36.140 - 00:20:36.980]

you can say

### [00:20:36.980 - 00:20:38.100]

in one given way.

### [00:20:39.540 - 00:20:40.140]

So for instance,

### [00:20:40.240 - 00:20:41.000]

when I provide

### [00:20:41.000 - 00:20:41.500]

a response

### [00:20:41.500 - 00:20:42.260]

to a given prompt,

### [00:20:42.900 - 00:20:43.700]

there can be

### [00:20:43.700 - 00:20:44.560]

very well a case

### [00:20:44.560 - 00:20:45.560]

where I can formulate

### [00:20:45.560 - 00:20:46.320]

the response

### [00:20:46.320 - 00:20:47.540]

slightly differently,

### [00:20:48.340 - 00:20:49.140]

but it will still

### [00:20:49.140 - 00:20:49.900]

be just as good.

### [00:20:49.900 - 00:20:53.260]

So the idea

### [00:20:53.260 - 00:20:54.280]

behind these metrics

### [00:20:54.280 - 00:20:55.940]

is to make

### [00:20:55.940 - 00:20:56.680]

this comparison

### [00:20:56.680 - 00:20:58.380]

a little bit

### [00:20:58.380 - 00:20:58.740]

flexible.

### [00:21:01.690 - 00:21:02.630]

So let's start

### [00:21:02.630 - 00:21:03.710]

with one common

### [00:21:03.710 - 00:21:04.430]

one that people

### [00:21:04.430 - 00:21:05.470]

use in the

### [00:21:05.470 - 00:21:06.570]

translation case.

### [00:21:06.990 - 00:21:07.570]

So this metric

### [00:21:07.570 - 00:21:08.230]

is called

### [00:21:08.230 - 00:21:09.290]

METEAR

### [00:21:09.290 - 00:21:10.870]

and it stands

### [00:21:10.870 - 00:21:11.550]

for metric

### [00:21:11.550 - 00:21:12.410]

for evaluation

### [00:21:12.410 - 00:21:13.110]

of translation

### [00:21:13.110 - 00:21:14.190]

with explicit ordering.

### [00:21:14.190 - 00:21:16.610]

So the idea

### [00:21:16.610 - 00:21:18.070]

here is

### [00:21:18.070 - 00:21:19.410]

to compare

### [00:21:19.410 - 00:21:21.090]

reference

### [00:21:21.090 - 00:21:22.610]

and predicted

### [00:21:22.610 - 00:21:24.190]

and we'll see

### [00:21:24.190 - 00:21:24.810]

how it's being

### [00:21:24.810 - 00:21:25.070]

done

### [00:21:25.070 - 00:21:27.290]

and also

### [00:21:27.290 - 00:21:29.770]

penalize

### [00:21:29.770 - 00:21:30.610]

cases

### [00:21:30.610 - 00:21:32.210]

when words

### [00:21:32.210 - 00:21:33.450]

are not

### [00:21:33.450 - 00:21:33.990]

in the same

### [00:21:33.990 - 00:21:34.370]

order,

### [00:21:34.810 - 00:21:35.930]

which is

### [00:21:35.930 - 00:21:37.090]

explaining why

### [00:21:37.090 - 00:21:38.210]

the metric is called

### [00:21:38.210 - 00:21:39.190]

with explicit

### [00:21:39.190 - 00:21:39.630]

ordering.

### [00:21:39.630 - 00:21:41.690]

So the formula

### [00:21:41.690 - 00:21:42.370]

is as follows.

### [00:21:42.690 - 00:21:43.550]

So it is

### [00:21:43.550 - 00:21:44.670]

some F score

### [00:21:44.670 - 00:21:46.430]

times one

### [00:21:46.430 - 00:21:47.370]

minus some

### [00:21:47.370 - 00:21:47.770]

penalty.

### [00:21:50.400 - 00:21:50.740]

So the

### [00:21:50.740 - 00:21:51.760]

F score

### [00:21:51.760 - 00:21:53.040]

here is

### [00:21:53.040 - 00:21:54.240]

so you may

### [00:21:54.240 - 00:21:54.640]

be familiar

### [00:21:54.640 - 00:21:55.600]

with F1 score.

### [00:21:56.000 - 00:21:56.420]

So it's like

### [00:21:56.420 - 00:21:57.040]

the harmonic

### [00:21:57.040 - 00:21:57.680]

mean with

### [00:21:57.680 - 00:21:58.980]

equal weights.

### [00:21:59.400 - 00:21:59.900]

So this one

### [00:21:59.900 - 00:22:00.360]

is with

### [00:22:00.360 - 00:22:01.140]

the variable

### [00:22:01.140 - 00:22:01.540]

weights.

### [00:22:02.380 - 00:22:03.100]

So it is

### [00:22:03.100 - 00:22:03.620]

a function

### [00:22:03.620 - 00:22:05.320]

of precision

### [00:22:05.320 - 00:22:06.200]

and recall

### [00:22:06.200 - 00:22:07.740]

where

### [00:22:07.740 - 00:22:08.400]

precision

### [00:22:08.400 - 00:22:09.200]

is

### [00:22:09.200 - 00:22:10.500]

the proportion

### [00:22:10.500 - 00:22:11.400]

of

### [00:22:11.400 - 00:22:12.480]

the

### [00:22:12.480 - 00:22:13.160]

unigrams

### [00:22:13.160 - 00:22:13.420]

that are

### [00:22:13.420 - 00:22:13.800]

in your

### [00:22:13.800 - 00:22:14.420]

predicted

### [00:22:14.420 - 00:22:16.280]

sequence

### [00:22:16.280 - 00:22:17.820]

that are

### [00:22:17.820 - 00:22:18.500]

matching

### [00:22:18.500 - 00:22:18.880]

with the

### [00:22:18.880 - 00:22:19.320]

reference

### [00:22:19.320 - 00:22:20.800]

and the

### [00:22:20.800 - 00:22:21.180]

recall

### [00:22:21.180 - 00:22:21.900]

is the

### [00:22:21.900 - 00:22:22.380]

proportion

### [00:22:22.380 - 00:22:22.880]

of the

### [00:22:22.880 - 00:22:23.440]

unigrams

### [00:22:23.440 - 00:22:23.720]

in the

### [00:22:23.720 - 00:22:24.500]

reference

### [00:22:24.500 - 00:22:26.540]

that are

### [00:22:26.540 - 00:22:27.020]

matching

### [00:22:27.020 - 00:22:27.880]

with what

### [00:22:27.880 - 00:22:28.120]

is in

### [00:22:28.120 - 00:22:28.220]

the

### [00:22:28.220 - 00:22:28.560]

predicted.

### [00:22:29.640 - 00:22:30.020]

So it's

### [00:22:30.020 - 00:22:30.280]

basically

### [00:22:30.280 - 00:22:30.840]

matching

### [00:22:30.840 - 00:22:31.560]

the

### [00:22:31.560 - 00:22:33.620]

usual

### [00:22:33.620 - 00:22:34.120]

precision

### [00:22:34.120 - 00:22:34.600]

recall

### [00:22:34.600 - 00:22:35.000]

metrics

### [00:22:35.000 - 00:22:35.360]

that you

### [00:22:35.360 - 00:22:35.500]

know.

### [00:22:36.760 - 00:22:37.140]

And then

### [00:22:37.140 - 00:22:37.780]

we have

### [00:22:37.780 - 00:22:38.660]

another

### [00:22:38.660 - 00:22:39.780]

quantity

### [00:22:39.780 - 00:22:40.120]

here,

### [00:22:40.120 - 00:22:40.380]

which is

the

### [00:22:40.520 - 00:22:40.880]

penalty

### [00:22:40.880 - 00:22:41.240]

and I

### [00:22:41.240 - 00:22:41.520]

mentioned

### [00:22:41.520 - 00:22:41.740]

the

### [00:22:41.740 - 00:22:42.040]

penalty

### [00:22:42.040 - 00:22:42.560]

here

### [00:22:42.560 - 00:22:43.680]

tries

### [00:22:43.680 - 00:22:43.940]

to

### [00:22:43.940 - 00:22:44.980]

incentivize

### [00:22:44.980 - 00:22:46.040]

good

### [00:22:46.040 - 00:22:47.280]

ordering.

### [00:22:47.640 - 00:22:47.960]

So if

### [00:22:47.960 - 00:22:48.180]

it's

### [00:22:48.180 - 00:22:48.560]

ordered

### [00:22:48.560 - 00:22:48.820]

the

same

in

and

in
